analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free is caused by stale ownership in Variant unwrapping of ExtensionObject. In Variant_decodeBinaryUnwrapExtensionObject, a temporary NodeId (typeId) is decoded and then assigned into dst->type selection logic. On the successful unwrap path (known type + ByteString encoding), the function does not release/reset typeId before decoding payload into dst->data. During nested decoding, ExtensionObject_decodeBinary may free NodeId members that alias the same underlying string/bytes memory, leaving a dangling pointer later copied by UA_copy/UA_Array_copy (seen as UAF in NodeId_copy -> UA_String_copy). Root cause is incorrect lifetime/cleanup handling of decoded NodeId/embedded members in the unwrap path, not the later memcpy crash site.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered by fuzz_binary_decode when input decodes a Variant containing ExtensionObject(s) with ByteString-encoded payload and crafted nested content that causes NodeId/String allocation and subsequent member deletion during decode. Data flow: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> tortureEncoding -> UA_decodeBinary(Variant/containing type) -> Variant_decodeBinaryUnwrapExtensionObject -> nested ExtensionObject_decodeBinary/Array_decodeBinary. The malformed binary must drive the unwrap path (known typeId + encoded ByteString) and then nested decode/cleanup so freed NodeId-backed memory is still referenced and later deep-copied by UA_copy.
